title: Execute complete synthetic Fourier transforms on physical tapes
body:
I complete the normalized synthetic Fourier interface W±/M on physical tapes. Earlier outer fixtures retained H/layout oracles and a bounded diagonal simulator. I use PR3627's arbitrary-support H endpoint in natural axis order, implement all-size signed polynomial rotations, batch the final per-axis bit reversal, and reuse one fixed inventory across the complete schedule.

I lift once to p+A precision for A address bits. Since the schedule contains exactly A normalized butterfly factors, I preserve exact intermediate grids and return Q_p(W±x/M) with one final truncation and coefficient error below sqrt(2) 2^-p. I include top/common rounds, support tails, both transform directions, output order and cleanup in the conditional time/space proof. For fixed D=Theta(p^epsilon), ell=Theta(p^(1-epsilon)) and A=Theta(p), I derive O(V p^(1-min(epsilon,.997)*.00172899) log p) time and O(V)+F_q space under the retained supplier/refinement premises.

I passed all seven registered suites, source-history/committed-byte checks and metadata validation. I check 640 encoded exponents, complete forward/opposite packets, support batching, changed-shape owner reuse, two endpoint batches and nine failure controls against a separate dense polynomial oracle. I exported commit `f9688868f4cf32ddb9a9bbfed402404a3d0ecb11`; the Git-free replay and hosted CI remain in progress. I will add those receipts before marking this draft ready.

The complete packets use the declared q=2 fixture and direct/literal root paths. I have not executed a production GL64/O(73,2) full Fourier payload. I do not claim an integer-multiplication exponent, a Gaussian/CRT/product/recovery join or supplier admission. Both normalized transforms divide by M; their composition is I/M. I leave the selected frontier unchanged.

I start from canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. I record the exact scope, five-point expansion decision and live overlap in TASK.json and the [existing investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2612#discussioncomment-19009513).

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including source-analysis agents. I credit OpenAI's source06 and Nick Petalas's all-size identity proof, Sagar Thakrar's PR3617, Chris/Clear1nsight's PR3623, PR3627/3619/3599 and their retained native, routing, Compact, compiler and normalization notices. I name the contributors and exact pins in the README. I claim no independent human or formal-kernel review. Apache-2.0.
